subject: tu:game/ui/select
value: The PAD-HARVEST re-census confirms that NONE of select.c's run-5 blockers were reached by the P1 25-field or shop 8-field waves: 0x333C, 0x3348-0x3358, 0xA8B-0xA8E and 0x1ECC all still sit inside pad_333C[4], pad_3348[0x14], pad_0A88[0x34C] and pad_1ECC[0x354] as of 2026-08-31. 132 of select.c's 137 remaining bare Player sites are blocked on exactly four pad runs, and two of them are FULLY accounted for with zero unknown bytes, so a header-extension pass can split them with byte-accounting proof rather than guesswork. RUN pad_3348[0x14] = 0x3348..0x335B, exactly five s32 words, all five in use, 109 select.c sites, all read+write, plus a four-word reset block in game/game/player.c lines 3432-3435 (0x334C=0, 0x3350=0, 0x3354=0, 0x3358=-1) which is the same teardown-zero-block evidence class the P1 wave used: (a) 0x3348, 66 sites, s32, the memcard/save sub-menu step-and-timer word -- switched on as a state selector, stepped with += 1, accumulated with += gFrameTicks and compared against 0x78 and 0x460, driven NEGATIVE with -= gFrameTicks and compared against -0x78, set to -1 on any failure and to 1000 on the out-of-space branch; (b) 0x334C, 22 sites, s32, memcard CHANNEL -- first argument of saveMount(chan, slot, 1), saveGetFreeBytes(chan, slot), MemCardCreateGaunt(chan, slot) and add_vmu_file(chan, slot, file, name, flags, character), and a *4 index into lbl_80344A14/lbl_80344A18; (c) 0x3350, 22 sites, s32, memcard SLOT -- second argument of the same four calls, always paired with 0x334C; (d) 0x3354, 6 sites, s32, save-FILE index -- third argument of add_vmu_file and the sole argument of PlayerLoadSaveFile(i, X) / PlayerWriteSaveFile(i, X), and a *16 index into lbl_80274578; (e) 0x3358, 5 sites, s32, the file-list menu CURSOR -- written together with 0x3354 as choice - 1000, set to -1 on cancel, and copied straight into OPTMENU.sel by setup_sel_menu. Splitting this one 0x14-byte run into five s32 fields unblocks 109 sites in select.c alone and is the single highest-value header edit available. RUN pad_333C[4] = one s32, 14 select.c sites plus two zeroing sites in player.c (lines 3244, 3471): it is a saved copy of Player.motion_state (0x3338) -- do_player_select stashes motion_state into it on entry to a sub-menu and restores motion_state from it at every sub-menu exit, and writes a literal 1 on the locked-in path. Fully evidenced, zero unknown bytes. RUN pad_0A88[0x34C] = 0xA88..0xDD3, partially mapped: 0xA8B is an s8 flag (select.c tests != 0 twice to pick the 1-vs-0 initial sub-menu state; player.c line 3405 sets it to -1 and line 3830 to 0; gamemain.c line 3774 clears it) sitting 3 bytes past the end of char name[8] at 0xA80, which is worth checking against the possibility that the GC name field is longer than 8 bytes; 0xA8C is a u16 unlocked-character bitmask read at 5 select.c sites as mask & (1 << (respawn_char - 8)), i.e. it gates PlayerCharType 8..15 only; 0xA8E is a u16 written by player.c line 3971 from a running total and passed as add_vmu_file's flags argument; and 0xA90 begins a 16-entry 24-byte array (0xA90..0xC0F) already modelled by select.c's file-local ClassStatSlot view (exp@0 fed to ExpToLevel, f32@8/0xC/0x10/0x14 feeding stats rows 0/2/3/1), reached as pl + sel * 24 + 2704. RUN pad_1ECC[0x354] is NOT unknown space: game/game/gamemain.c line 3802 does *(PlayerSaveBlk*)(p + 7884) = *(PlayerSaveBlk*)(p + 2688), a 5172-byte (0x1434) struct assignment copying [0xA80, 0x1EB4) onto [0x1ECC, 0x3300), and game/game/player.c line 3468 clears the destination with memset(p + 0x1ECC, 0, 0x1434). select.c performs the same assignment once. So Player carries a byte-for-byte SHADOW of its whole persistent block, and pad_1ECC's size 0x354 is exactly name[8] + pad_0A88[0x34C] -- the shadow of the live 0xA80..0xDD4 region. HYPOTHESIS FOR THE NEXT WAVE TO CHECK, NOT ADOPTED HERE: under that mapping char_save[16] at 0xDD4 shadows to 0xDD4 + 0x144C = 0x2220 exactly, which is where the header currently documents crystals[8] / gargoyle_items[3] / legend_items[2], and field_224C lands at char_save[0] + 0x2C. Either those names describe the shadow of the progression block rather than independent counters, or the copy is not the only writer of that region; the arithmetic is exact and the coincidence is worth resolving before any further field is added between 0x1ECC and 0x2250. options.c's sole Player-pad blocker is PlayerCharSave pad_10[4]: next_boss_hint reads two u16 boss-crystal bitmasks at slot +0x10 and +0x12 (absolute 0xDE4 / 0xDE6), tested as 1 << crystal_order[boss_hint_index] to select a pass-1 vs pass-2 hint tier. Per claim.law.embedded-struct-member-whole-tu-cascade every addition listed here is a SCALAR or an array of scalars, so the aggregate-member cascade class does not apply to any of them.
